## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

The new exclusion flag should honor `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` so CI jobs can configure which files their archives omit.

## Changes

The archive CLI adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that matches filenames and logs skipped paths in verbose mode. The pull request also adds flag documentation, tests, and a review fixture.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the exclusion default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and no `--exclude` argument, `app.log` still enters the archive. The parser hardcodes an empty default, while `.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` requires each new flag to “take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable.” — CI jobs that configure exclusions through the environment produce archives containing files they intended to omit.

## Suggestions

- cli/main.py:33 — tests — Test basename matching in nested directories — For `logs/skip.log` and `--exclude skip.log`, the suite would miss a regression that matches the relative path and keeps the file. Every exclusion test with real files places them directly under the source directory. — Exact-name exclusions could stop working for nested files without failing the suite.
- tests/test_main.py:20 — tests — Assert repeated exclusions in the resulting archive — With `--exclude '*.log' --exclude '*.tmp'`, this test passes even if the CLI applies only the first glob. It checks the parsed list, while the archive test passes a single `--exclude`. — The suite would miss a CLI regression that leaves files matched by the second glob in the archive. — Fix: Extend `test_main_leaves_excluded_files_out_of_the_archive` to cover repeated flags.
